sections.title: The short version
paras: US aid to Israel is mostly military financing that must be spent in the United States. It flows from taxpayers, through Congress and the Pentagon, to American weapons makers, and arrives in Israel as hardware.

It is not charity, and it is not a pure gift to Israel either: it serves US defense industry and US strategy at the same time. The record also shows Washington can attach conditions — and has, a handful of times.

two_systems.title: US ⇄ Israel: Two Systems Compared
two_systems.sub: Scoped to what each government actually delivers to its own residents, Israel's system delivers more for its people than the US system does for its own — by a decisive margin (+1.21 of 5) — on an economy about 45× smaller in total. Decisively, not uniformly: the US wins two of eleven systems.

sections.title: The scorecard — 11 citizen-facing systems, scored 0–5
sections.cap: Each system scored from sourced figures in this module. Bars share one 0–5 scale.

sections.title: The defensible answer
paras: Scoped to direct citizen provision — healthcare, jobs, housing, the safety net, happiness, public safety, emergency response, education, debt burden, transportation, and infrastructure — Israel's system delivers more for its people than the US system does for its own, by a wide and decisive margin (+1.21 of 5), despite operating on a fraction of the US's total economic size.
The US's remaining strength is concentrated in national economic scale and institutional power — real, but a different achievement than serving its own residents better.

sections.title: Where the US still wins
paras: Two of eleven categories outright: Housing (Israel's public housing stock is shrinking while its waitlist grows) and Social Services/Poverty (Israel's own National Insurance Institute reports a higher poverty rate than the US official measure). The Israel lead is decisive, not uniform.

sections.title: The wartime caveat
paras: The composite describes structural system design. Israel's 2026 budget cut education, health, and welfare ministries by 3%+ to fund record defense spending — a real, current strain on exactly the systems scored highly. Both belong side by side.

sections.title: Two composites, two questions
sections.cap: Same underlying scores. The 21-system version adds Finance, Energy, Central Banking, Digital Infrastructure, Government Administration, Taxation, Telecommunications, Environment, and Immigration — measures of national economic and institutional scale, not citizen provision.

sections.title: Two corrections, stated plainly
paras: 1. Transportation and Construction & Infrastructure were first miscategorized as 'national scale' and excluded; adding them back narrowed an overstated gap.
2. Public Safety first rested on a decade-old Israeli incarceration figure; current same-methodology data (US 541 vs Israel 217 per 100k) widened the gap.
The corrections moved the number in opposite directions — what an honest process should look like.

sections.title: The equity pass
paras: Run on both sides: US Black poverty 18.4% (2.4× white), Black–white wealth gap 4.3×; Israel's Haredi poverty 32.8% and Arab poverty 37.6% vs ~21% nationally. The disparities are comparable in scale. A full equity sub-score wasn't applied, because doing it for one system only would itself be a bias.

sections.title: More money, shorter lives
sections.cap: The US spends about 3.7× as much per person and lives 4.8 years less. This is a system-design gap, not a resource gap.

sections.title: The design difference
paras: Israel's 1995 law enrolls every resident in one of four nonprofit health funds with the same government-set basic package — no deductibles, small flat copays. In the US, coverage is a patchwork tied mostly to employment: losing a job usually means losing insurance.

sections.title: The single biggest gap: losing your job
paras: Unemployment pay is similar — 40–60% of wages for about 26 weeks (US) vs ~60% for 138–175 days (Israel). The difference is health coverage: a laid-off Israeli's coverage simply continues. A laid-off American must choose between COBRA (up to 102% of the full premium), Medicaid, or a Marketplace plan within 60 days.

sections.title: Inequality inside each country
paras: US: the Black poverty rate is 18.4% — 2.4× the white rate — and the Black–white wealth gap is about 4.3×. Israel: deep poverty concentrates in Haredi and Arab communities. Both countries' averages hide large internal gaps.

sections.title: How to read this dashboard
paras: These are documented counts from named sources, each labeled. Israel disputes the Gaza Health Ministry's figures; the UN treats them as reliable, and two peer-reviewed studies found they likely undercount deaths.
Israeli lives are counted on their own tab with Israel's official figures and the same discipline. No toll is used to erase another.

sections.title: Reported deaths vs. independent estimates
sections.cap: Two peer-reviewed studies in The Lancet. Both found the reported count was lower than the true toll.

sections.title: What the studies did — and did not — settle
paras: The 2025 study used three independent lists (hospital records, a ministry survey, obituaries); the 2026 study was the first survey not relying on ministry records. Women, children, and the elderly were about 56% of violent deaths — roughly matching the ministry's breakdown. sections.title: The short version
paras: The state was financed before it was declared. A bank (1899), a land fund (1901), a permanent fundraising arm (1920), an American donor base (1921 onward), a deal that moved German Jewish capital (1933), and a wartime arms-buying network (1945) were all in place before May 1948.

The money came overwhelmingly from private donors and institutions — small givers through the blue box, wealthy Americans, and organized appeals — not from any government. Governments supplied something else: Britain's legal framework, and in 1948 Soviet-bloc weapons.

paras: It wasn't cheap — and it wasn't secret. sections.title: Claim by claim
rows: Egypt and Jordan refuse Palestinians because of terrorism
Security concerns exist; Jordan hosts ~2M refugees; Egypt refuses permanent displacement
Egypt sends no aid to Gaza
Rafah was a main route until Israel took it in May 2024
Jordan is the Palestinian state from the partition
Transjordan split off in 1922; partition was west of the river
~13–16 states restrict entry — but it's whataboutism
The West wouldn't take Jewish refugees
Name stolen from Rome to erase Judea
Rome renamed it c. 135 CE; the name was 500+ years older
Both from the 1916 Arab Revolt flag
Corruption real; IMF found diversion to Arafat-controlled accounts
Used by many Jewish groups; some users are antisemitic
Egypt's wall proves Muslims fear Muslims
Barrier exists — for tunnels and militants

sections.title: Two questions for any viral claim
steps: Find the primary source or a credible record.
A true fact can carry a false claim.
The missing context usually decides it.
